data_check.notes: The matchup hypothesis precedes this numerical check. Tuten's supplied totals imply 4.74 yards per carry and 14.33 carries per game over three games. At that observed efficiency, 13 carries would produce approximately 61.7 yards; this is a conditional sensitivity calculation, not a projection or simulation. CIN's 5.00 YPC allowed supports rather than contradicts the read. Over 57.5 at -114 requires approximately 53.27% to break even. The listed under is also -114, making the same-book proportional no-vig split 50% per side; that is not a Pinnacle benchmark or an estimated true probability. No calibrated hit probability or stake is justified.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and Tuten's over lost: Cincinnati's explosive passing created a lead before Jacksonville could establish sustained rushing volume. Rodriguez and Abdullah, who combined for 30 carries in the supplied three-game window, retained enough work to leave Tuten short of the necessary opportunities. Alternatively, CIN's 5.00 YPC allowed proved unstable over only three games, or missing line-health and weather information undermined efficiency. The counter-case keeps this a conditional lean rather than a strong play; the over survives the Jacksonville-lead flip but not the Cincinnati-breakaway flip.
